paper_diagnosis: Two ocular infections during conventional chemotherapy in acute lymphoblastic leukemia
disease_label_per_paper: Febrile neutropenia during ALL induction with grade IV mucositis, candidemia, central-line removal, and Candida retinitis
presentation_summary: A 49-year-old man presented with fever and pancytopenia and was diagnosed with B-cell common acute lymphoblastic leukemia by bone marrow and immunophenotyping.
During induction chemotherapy through a Hickman line, he developed grade IV mucositis and prolonged neutropenia below 0.2 x10^3/microL.
He had febrile neutropenia treated empirically with intravenous meropenem and vancomycin.
Blood culture grew Candida albicans; caspofungin was added and the central line was removed.
Fever persisted for 2 weeks despite antimicrobials; retinal examination showed focal retinitis consistent with Candida involvement, prompting switch to intravenous amphotericin B.
